description: §6.7.1a — the SILENT-DROP guard. `@status = risky() !{ | _ e -> { @flag = "arm-ran" } }` (reactive-assign binding + a `-> { }` BLOCK arm) is the one `!{}` mount shape that COMPILED on baseline bc51b610 yet SILENTLY DROPPED the arm — the string rewriter emitted `_scrml_reactive_set("status", risky())` and discarded the `!{}` block entirely, so the arm's side effect (@flag = "arm-ran") never ran and @flag stayed "none". No E-CODEGEN, no diagnostic — a silent error-handling loss. Post-fix the mount body routes through the real statement codegen and the arm's block runs at mount. No input — the boot/mount shape.
rationale: §6.7.1a sugar-equivalence — a `!{}` handler inside `on mount` must execute exactly as inside a `function` body; it must not be silently discarded. risky() fails; the wildcard block arm runs, writing @flag = "arm-ran". The pin catches the specific silent-drop regression (arm dropped ⇒ @flag stays "none").
